source.title: Stabilizing brain-computer interfaces through alignment of latent dynamics

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed, verified via PubMed (PMID 40389429) and full text (PMC12089531). METADATA CORRECTION to the thought's reference list: the venue is Nature Communications 16:4662 (19 May 2025), not 'Nature Biomedical Engineering / open manuscript record' as the thought's bibliography states; the 2022 bioRxiv (10.1101/2022.04.06.487388) is the preprint. The claim in the thought -- alignment is more stable when temporal dynamics constrain the mapping rather than treating each state as an independent point -- is the paper's own framing and is backed by large effects (isometric-force task: median R2 0.91 and 208-day half-life for NoMAD vs 0.65/77 days for ADAN and 0.59/45 days for aligned factor analysis, zero failures vs 51 for aligned FA). Held at 0.6 because the alignment is of the SAME region's recordings across days to a fixed LFADS dynamics model, not a bridge between two independently specialised systems; MECH-539's cross-system transition-compatibility criterion is analogous, not identical.
failure_signatures: MECH-539 predicts a bridge that matches states pointwise can still scramble action-conditioned transitions; NoMAD's comparators (ADAN, aligned FA) are exactly pointwise, per-time-step alignments and they degrade faster and fail more often -- if a REE bridge ladder found the pointwise rungs as stable as the dynamics-constrained rung, this analogy would be broken.

The authors state the method assumes a stable manifold and consistent behaviour and has only been tested on single behaviours; a REE interface between two systems that are BOTH learning violates the first assumption on both sides.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Existing unsupervised iBCI stabilisation methods 'treat each time step as an independent sample and do not account for latent dynamics'. NoMAD instead aligns the distribution of an RNN (LFADS) generator's states between Day 0 and Day K -- KL divergence between fitted Gaussians on generator states plus a Poisson spike-reconstruction term, core dynamics frozen -- and achieves decoding 'with sustained stability over weeks- to months-long periods without supervised recalibration', substantially outperforming per-time-step alignment methods.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-539 says an interface between predictive systems must preserve transition geometry, not just pointwise state, and that pointwise-good/rollout-bad bridges are a real failure class. NoMAD is the engineering demonstration that constraining an alignment by a dynamics model makes it markedly more stable than pointwise alignment of the same data. The REE diagnostic it motivates -- map only the initial state and let the receiver evolve natively, versus re-mapping every step -- is a direct analogue of aligning to a generator's dynamics rather than to its samples.
mapping.mapping_caveat: NoMAD aligns one population to ITSELF across sessions against a frozen dynamics model; MECH-539 concerns a mapping BETWEEN two different systems each with its own dynamics. The stability gain here comes from a shared, fixed generator, which is precisely what two independently specialised REE modules do not have. Treat as motivation for the criterion, not as evidence that cross-system dynamic compatibility is achievable.
mapping.source_context: Monkey M1 Utah-array recordings (isometric wrist force, 20 sessions over 95 days; centre-out reaching, 12 sessions over 38 days) plus one human iBCI participant (T11, two sessions); offline decoding.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue and effect sizes, released code (snel-repo/nomad) and data (Dryad). Mapping and transfer both mid because the within-system/cross-system distinction is exactly the one MECH-539 is about.
